title: Servo Motor Position Calculation

placement_source.note: Superseded the old edge26/edge34 (Middle_Plate.Shape.Edges[25]/[33]) index-based derivation. BRep edge indices are not stable after topology edits, and the old derivation produced a stale pitch=90 deg convention that does not match the live document's identity rotation. The live document models the servo as two independently-placed Mesh::Feature objects (visual + collision-proxy) under App::Part "STS3032_Mount"; both were synced to this identical placement this session, so visual_placement and collision_placement are recorded separately above even though they currently hold the same values.

clearance_note: The top_plate/bottom_plate figures above (and the matching entries in validations[]) are from this Phase 2 script's coarse Z-height-only formula (see schema_note); it does not account for each plate's individual rotation, so bottom_plate was misreported as failing the 5.0mm nominal minimum here. Phase 3 (03_link_servo_to_assembly.py) was corrected in issue #22 to measure real 3D shape distance (Part.Shape.distToShape against a servo bounding-box proxy) instead: the real measured clearance is ~17.1mm to Bottom_Plate and ~6.43mm to Top_Plate, both comfortably passing the 5.0mm minimum. This Phase 2 JSON is left as originally generated for traceability; see servo_link_config.json for the corrected Phase 3 values.

validations.details: Clearance: 4.85mm (minimum: 5.0mm) -- coarse Z-only check, see clearance_note

schema_note: pitch/z_offset no longer have one consistent meaning: Top_Plate, Middle_Plate and Bottom_Plate each sit at their own independently Z-axis-rotated placement and Z height (6mm / 4mm / 3mm) rather than a uniform parallel stack. For this mount point the servo uses an identity rotation and an explicit (x, y, z), not an offset applied along a shared plate normal.
